2944052904a3f1d170c46769c9c1fa5d7be23118.summary: Free decryptor page from Emsisoft, published 2016-12-23, for GlobeImposter ransomware. GlobeImposter is a copycat of the Globe ransomware kit that imitates its ransom notes and file extension. Encrypted files get a .crypt extension and keep their base name. Decryption needs a matching pair of an encrypted file and its unencrypted original. The tools may not work on all ransomware versions and are provided without warranty.

29f0d3fb11935b6922316bd01163d21b625f9ab5.summary: Malpedia family page for Hades, a ransomware family. PCrisk describes Hades Locker as an updated version of WildFire Locker that encrypts many file types with AES. The page lists 17 dated reports from 2021 to 2025 by vendors and researchers including Sentinel LABS, Mandiant, CrowdStrike, Secureworks and Accenture. Named actors include Evil Corp, UNC2165 and GOLD WINTER. Tools named include Cobalt Strike, Meterpreter and MimiKatz. The page notes there is no YARA signature yet.

29b89bf0badf1497f496ad30ad9c25d67b5f650a.summary: EclecticIQ describes a campaign targeting the semiconductor industry in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore, using a HyperBro loader variant that side-loads a Cobalt Strike beacon through a signed CyberArk binary. A malware downloader fetches second-stage files from a compromised Cobra DocGuard server, and a Go backdoor named ChargeWeapon is also described. EclecticIQ assesses with high confidence that a PRC-backed nation-state actor is very likely behind the activity, citing overlaps with reporting on APT27, Carderbee and RedHotel.

290272a88e698dd38704ee5ba24b71324c95562a.summary: News article (9 Mar 2022) reporting an FBI alert that the Ragnar Locker ransomware gang has infected at least 52 critical infrastructure organizations in the US across several sectors. It describes double extortion, selective folder-exclusion encryption, shadow copy deletion, and a locale check that ends the infection on certain countries. The page also carries unrelated news items.
